solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tough nut playing charades

indicators.note: the letters of charades are played about with, as in a game, so they rearrange

explanation.surface: A stubborn person is having a game of charades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' signals rearranging all eight letters of CHARADES.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough nut is a hard, uncompromising person, and a hard case is the same kind of toughened character.

clue.text: Army entertainer

definitions.meaning: a great multitude, especially an army in older usage
someone who receives and entertains guests at a party

explanation.surface: Someone who entertains the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a large armed throng and a person who welcomes visitors into their home.

clue.text: Water settling in drainpipe

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the word drainpipe, settled among its letters

explanation.surface: Water collecting in a drainpipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settling in' says the answer lies within dRAINpipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainfall is water falling from clouds, so it can stand for water generally.

clue.text: Tory pamphlet editor shortened

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the party whose members are called Tories
a tract is a short polemical pamphlet

explanation.surface: A Conservative's leaflet has been cut by the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something contracted has been reduced in length or size, as a word with letters dropped.

clue.text: Work hard to loosen rivets

indicators.note: loosening the rivets lets their letters come apart and rearrange

explanation.surface: Labouring to work some rivets free.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive is to make great efforts, toiling hard at a task.

clue.text: Support Lincoln Town at the outset

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of US President Abraham Lincoln

indicators.note: only the very start of the word Town is wanted

explanation.surface: Backing Lincoln Town football club from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln City, not Town, is the real football club; 'Lincoln' is Abraham Lincoln, and 'at the outset' takes the T of Town.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage someone, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Titled lady one's seen in watering holes

indicators.note: the word one's is spotted inside the drinking places

parts.note: pubs and bars are jocularly called watering holes
taken as written, ONES

explanation.surface: A noblewoman is spotted in the pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is the containment signal; 'watering holes' is light-hearted slang for pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A baroness is a woman holding a peerage rank, a lady with a title.

clue.text: Revolutionary hated the former PM

indicators.note: a revolutionary overturns things, so the letters that follow are overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebel loathed the ex-prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel; it rearranges HATED THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Heath was the British Conservative Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974.

clue.text: People in the wrong to entrap first of poisonous spiders?

indicators.note: the sinners catch a letter inside them

parts.note: sinners are those who have done wrong

indicators.note: only the opening letter of poisonous is taken

explanation.surface: Wrongdoers catching poisonous spiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to entrap' puts P, the 'first of' poisonous, inside SINNERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiders spin webs, so they are whimsically spinning creatures; the question mark flags the playful sense.

clue.text: Raised money, some might have said

indicators.note: the word is spoken rather than spelt, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Money was raised, according to some people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some might have said' signals a word that sounds like BREAD, slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Bred means brought up or reared, as children or animals are raised.

clue.text: Lad sure out to get thrashed, playing away

indicators.note: a thrashing knocks things about, so the letters are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: A cocky lad is set to lose heavily in an away fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get thrashed' rearranges LAD SURE OUT. The sporting surface hides the slang sense of 'playing away'.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing away is a British idiom for being unfaithful to one's partner, which is what an adulterous person does.

clue.text: One day in southern French region to make fortune

indicators.note: the two letters are placed inside the region's name

parts.note: Provence is a region in the south-east of France
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A day trip in the south of France to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence means fate or divine guidance, the force behind one's luck.

clue.text: Epic film about a twice-married person

indicators.note: the outer pieces go around the little word a

parts.note: an epic is something big in scale
a film is a thin layer, like a mist on glass

explanation.surface: A big movie about a man with two wives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' wants to be a movie, matching 'Epic', but here it is a thin haze; 'about' wraps the two around the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigamist marries a second spouse while still wed to the first.

clue.text: Horse to follow tailless wild cat

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is cut off

parts.note: to stalk is to follow stealthily
a lion is a big wild cat

explanation.surface: A horse pursuing a big cat with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' applies to STALK, not the cat: drop its K to leave STAL, then add LION.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male horse.

clue.text: I make move to keep holy books undamaged

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the scripture abbreviation within

parts.note: to act is to make a move or take action
NT is the New Testament, the later books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone acting while keeping sacred texts safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' is the containment signal; 'holy books' is the usual crossword shorthand for the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Intact describes something whole and unharmed.

clue.text: Small room near rear of apartment

parts.note: close means near

indicators.note: only the back letter of apartment is taken

explanation.surface: A little room by the back of a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear of' takes the T of apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a cupboard or small private chamber.

clue.text: Place to find 13? Sure

definitions.meaning: a building where horses such as the stallion of 13 are kept
steady and firm, not likely to give way

explanation.surface: Asking where a stallion is kept, then confirming.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a horse's building and something firm and steady.

clue.text: Adapted wall heater suitable for any climate

indicators.note: the heater is modified, so the letters of wall heater are reworked

explanation.surface: A modified wall heater that works in every climate.
explanation.definitionFit: All-weather gear or pitches can be used whatever the conditions outdoors.

clue.text: Sharif, say, taking leads in old movies and romcoms

indicators.note: the leading letters of each of the next four words are taken

explanation.surface: An actor named Sharif starring in old films and romantic comedies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads in' takes the first letters of old, movies, and, romcoms; 'leads' looks like starring roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Omar Sharif was an Egyptian film star, so he exemplifies people with this first name.

clue.text: Cold, boy dressed

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A chilly boy wearing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad means clothed or covered, an older past participle of clothe.

clue.text: Bird, black, is spotted on island

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A black bird is seen on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted on' places B and IS after the I for island.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a curved bill.

clue.text: Lab rebuilt round ruined manor? That's strange

indicators.note: the reworked lab letters go around the reworked manor
the word Lab is reconstructed, so its letters are reordered
the manor is wrecked, so its letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A laboratory rebuilt around a ruined manor house is an odd sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams, signalled by 'rebuilt' and 'ruined'; 'round' then puts the second inside the first, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormal means departing from what is usual, so odd or unusual.

clue.text: To New York for an award

explanation.surface: Heading to New York for a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tony is the annual prize for Broadway theatre, held in New York.

clue.text: Having lots of free time, I certainly will get taken round about

indicators.note: the guided word goes about the others, enclosing them

parts.note: someone guided or shown round has been led
sure means certainly

explanation.surface: Someone with plenty of free time being given a tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes the guided word enclose the rest, which sit just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisured people have ample spare time, free of the need to work.
